en.title: The participle
en.summary: English has a present participle in -ing and a past participle.

paragraphs: A participle is a verb form that works as part of a verb phrase or as an adjective. English has a present participle ending in -ing and a past participle, which ends in -ed for regular verbs and is irregular for many common ones.

items: She is **reading**. It was **written** by hand.

blocks.html:
UseExample
continuous tensesShe is reading. They were playing.
perfect tensesI have finished. He had gone.
passiveThe door was closed.
adjective before a nounan interesting book, a closed door
reduced clauseThe man standing there is my uncle.
reason or timeFeeling tired, he went to bed.

paragraphs: Some adjectives have both forms with different meanings. The -ing form describes the thing or person that causes the feeling; the -ed form describes the person who has the feeling.

blocks.html:
-ing (causing)-ed (feeling)
The film was boring.I was bored.
It is an exciting game.We are excited.
a surprising resultsurprised people
tiring worktired workers

items: Wrong: **I am boring.** (if you mean you feel bored) Right: **I am bored.**
Wrong: **a break window** Right: **a broken window**
Wrong: **He has wrote.** Right: **He has written.**
Wrong: **Walking along the street, the rain began.** Right: **Walking along the street, I felt the rain.** (the participle must refer to the same subject)
